subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: GW_Well: a shaft or hole sunk, dug or drilled into the Earth to observe, extract or inject water (SAWGraph's rendering of GWML2, imports/gwml2_hyfo_terms.ttl); a lulcw:Piezometer is a BSS monitoring point of the network
counterexample_considered: Some monitoring points are springs (Fontestramar 10795X0001/S, Source de la Tirounère, Source Sainte-Cécile, Source Clots de Rhodes): not drilled wells, so no subclass

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: Withdrawn 2026-11-06: the springs of the network are lulcw:Piezometer instances

subject: lulcw:Piezometer
definition_comparison: hyfo:WaterWell: a water well, with focus on the hole/shaft itself; a lulcw:Piezometer is a BSS monitoring point
counterexample_considered: The springs of the network are not wells

subject: lulcw:MonitoringStation
definition_comparison: GW_MonitoringSite: site of observation related to groundwater; a lulcw:MonitoringStation is a station of the ADES groundwater-level network
counterexample_considered: A station hosted by a spring is still a monitoring site: none found
reviewer: Claude (2026-10-24, rechecked 2026-11-06), to review by Assil

subject: lulcw:hostedBy
definition_comparison: gwMonitoringHost: identifies the feature hosting the site, e.g. a well, spring, lake or stream; lulcw:hostedBy links a station to its piezometer
counterexample_considered: A spring host is explicitly allowed by GWML2: none

subject: lulcw:HydrogeologicalUnit
definition_comparison: GW_HydrogeoUnit: any soil or rock unit or zone that by virtue of its hydraulic properties has a distinct influence on the storage or movement of groundwater; a BD LISA entity is one
counterexample_considered: An impermeable BD LISA entity still influences the movement of groundwater (GW_AquiferUnit includes confining beds): none found

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: Entailed through lulcw:HydrogeologicalUnit
counterexample_considered: None

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: GW_Aquifer: a body of earth material that contains (or potentially contains) sufficient saturated permeable material to yield significant quantities of water to wells and springs; the written mapping rule types the alluvium units as alluvial aquifers
counterexample_considered: A locally confined alluvial unit (CQ14) is still an aquifer: none found

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above; the written rule types the karst units as karst aquifers
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: GW_AquiferSystem: a body of permeable and poorly permeable material that functions regionally as a water-yielding unit (two or more permeable beds separated by confining beds); the Pliocene multilayer (671AA00) by the written rule
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: An impermeable mapped unit is not an aquifer
counterexample_considered: Its confining role is local; neither GW_Aquifer nor GW_ConfiningBed is asserted

subject: lulcw:monitors
definition_comparison: tapsAquifer: identifies the aquifer a well taps (no domain or range declared); lulcw:monitors links a piezometer to the unit it monitors
counterexample_considered: A spring monitors the unit it drains: consistent

subject: lulcw:pumpsFrom
definition_comparison: As above; lulcw:pumpsFrom links an abstraction facility to the unit it pumps from
counterexample_considered: None found

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: SWEET's Aquifer is broader and differently axiomatised
counterexample_considered: No subclass or equivalence asserted

subject: lulcw:KarstAquifer
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:MultilayerAquiferSystem
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:ConfiningUnit
definition_comparison: SWEET's Aquitard: a confining bed; a mapped impermeable unit is a candidate
counterexample_considered: As above

subject: lulcw:AlluvialAquifer
definition_comparison: Confinement is a local assessment (CQ14)
counterexample_considered: Parts of an alluvial unit can be confined under a clay cover

subject: lulcw:Watercourse
definition_comparison: HY_River: a body of surface water, participating in a hydrographic network, that permanently or temporarily flows; a lulcw:Watercourse is a river identified by its BD Carthage code
counterexample_considered: A canal coded as a watercourse would not qualify: the graph's watercourses are the gauged and documented rivers, and canal reaches carry no watercourse

subject: lulcw:RiverReach
definition_comparison: HY_FlowPath realizes a catchment as a path connecting its inflow and outflow; a river reach is a mapped segment of the network between two nodes
counterexample_considered: The graph holds no catchment that a reach would realise: a close match, not a subclass

subject: lulcw:HydrographicReach
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: Withdrawn 2026-11-06 (Codex review, R3): a canal reach conveys diverted water across catchments and realises none

subject: lulcw:CanalReach
definition_comparison: As above
counterexample_considered: A canal reach realises no catchment

subject: lulcw:SurfaceWaterBody
definition_comparison: HY_WaterBody: water standing in a depression or flowing in a channel; a WFD river water body is a management delimitation of stretches
counterexample_considered: None needed: the meanings differ
